decisions.subject: Pipeline for the Brunswick v3 revision

options_considered.label: cinematic
options_considered.reason: Mood-led montage built from supplied stills with a music-only bed — exactly this pipeline's remit, and it gates proposal/script/scene_plan/assets so the client sees the shot list before render.

options_considered.label: hybrid
options_considered.reason: Designed for source footage plus support visuals.
options_considered.rejected_because: There is no video source and no support visuals to generate; the extra machinery buys nothing.

options_considered.label: animation
options_considered.reason: Motion-graphics-first.
options_considered.rejected_because: The deliverable is photography-led; an animation pipeline would fight the material.

decisions.reason: Still-led, music-only, mood-driven brand montage from client-supplied photography.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime for the v3 render

options_considered.label: Remotion (React scene components)
options_considered.reason: All nine beats are stills needing precise, individually-parameterised Ken Burns moves plus a typographic overlay that must sit identically on every beat. React props over a frame counter make that exact and repeatable, and the outro's staggered type reveal is straightforward with spring physics. Was NOT available at session start (node_modules missing); installed during preflight and re-verified as available.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP)
options_considered.reason: Genuinely available and genuinely good here — the outro is typographic and GSAP would express the staggered reveal naturally. Tradeoff: the nine photo beats are the bulk of the piece and are image-transform work, not typography, so HyperFrames' strength applies to about four seconds of a twenty-six second video.

options_considered.label: FFmpeg zoompan concat
options_considered.reason: Always available and would handle the Ken Burns beats.
options_considered.rejected_because: Cannot produce a designed, animated outro — it would force a static PNG end card, which is the one thing the client explicitly asked to change.

decisions.reason: Recommended pending client approval. Both Remotion and HyperFrames are available on this machine and both were presented. Remotion wins on weight of work: nine parameterised still-motion beats dominate the runtime, and the redesigned outro is well within what Remotion can express. HyperFrames is the honest runner-up and would be the pick if the piece were mostly kinetic typography.

decisions.subject: Authoring mode for the composition

options_considered.label: Hand-authored composition
options_considered.reason: The brief is a redesign request on a brand deliverable. The outro in particular has to be new, not a restyled stock card.

options_considered.label: Stock cut.type scene catalog
options_considered.reason: Fast and reliable.
options_considered.rejected_because: text_card/hero_title would produce another centred contact slate — the exact thing being replaced. Templated cannot satisfy the ask.

decisions.reason: The client asked for a redesign; a template cannot deliver one. Costs more build time, which is disclosed in the proposal.

decisions.subject: Music bed for v3

options_considered.label: Reuse the music bed extracted from the approved v2 render
options_considered.reason: Already client-approved, keeps v3 in the same series, free, and available right now. Extracted at 22.17s, -13.5 dB mean / -0.4 dB peak; will need a loop-extend or hold to cover a ~26s runtime.

options_considered.label: Track from music_library/
options_considered.reason: Checked — the folder does not exist on this machine and holds no tracks.

options_considered.label: Generate a new track via a music API
options_considered.reason: Registry reports music_generation 0 of 3 configured — no provider has credentials.
options_considered.rejected_because: No music-generation provider is configured; this path is blocked, not merely expensive.

options_considered.label: pixabay_music search
options_considered.reason: music_search reports pixabay_music as available, so a royalty-free track could be sourced.
options_considered.rejected_because: Swapping the track changes the character of an already-approved piece; not requested by the client.

options_considered.label: No music
options_considered.reason: Silent montage.
options_considered.rejected_because: v2 is music-led and the cut is paced to the bed.

decisions.reason: Recommended pending approval. It is the only free, already-approved option, and the client asked for three specific changes — none of them audio.

decisions.subject: Creative direction for v3

options_considered.label: Room to Room
options_considered.reason: Fixes the tricycle frame and the bathroom-heavy weighting in one move, using frames that already exist.

options_considered.label: Before the Finish
options_considered.reason: Gives the edit a real arc.
options_considered.rejected_because: The folder's 'before' frames are empty rooms, not construction — the before/after turn would under-deliver on its own promise.

options_considered.label: Material Study
options_considered.reason: Uses the strongest photography in the set.
options_considered.rejected_because: The detail frames are almost all bathroom, so it would worsen the room imbalance the revision exists to fix, and cuts against the brand rule on standalone bathroom marketing.

decisions.reason: Recommended pending approval — the only concept that serves the stated request and the brand rule at the same time.

decisions.subject: Replacement frame for the living-room beat containing a child's tricycle

options_considered.label: finished-living-room-media-wall-view.png
options_considered.reason: Same room, same warm floor and wall tone as the rejected frame, shot from the opposite side. No tricycle, no coffee-table clutter, no floor cord, rug squared to the room. Native 2304x1536, so it crops to 16:9 with room to spare.

options_considered.label: finished-living-room-window-wall-wide.png
options_considered.reason: Clean French-door wall with strong daylight.
options_considered.rejected_because: A corner of the sofa intrudes at frame left and the room reads emptier — better as a second living-room beat than as the replacement.

options_considered.label: east_brunswick_11_living_room.png
options_considered.reason: Graded to match the rest of the east_brunswick set and also tricycle-free.
options_considered.rejected_because: The sofa dominates the foreground and the room reads as furniture rather than architecture.

options_considered.label: Keep the v2 frame
options_considered.reason: No work.

decisions.reason: Closest match to the frame being replaced, so it slots in with no grade break, while removing every object the client objected to.

decisions.subject: Style playbook

options_considered.label: clean-professional
options_considered.reason: Matches the restrained, warm, type-light grammar v2 already established and the brand's black-and-gold palette.

options_considered.label: premium-minimalist
options_considered.reason: Would suit the detail photography.
options_considered.rejected_because: Pulls toward the c3 material-study direction, which is not the selected concept.

options_considered.label: flat-motion-graphics
options_considered.reason: Pipeline's nominal default.
options_considered.rejected_because: Graphic, high-energy motion would be wrong over architectural photography and off-brand for this firm.

decisions.reason: Preserves series continuity with v2 while leaving room for the new outro.
